description: Deep learning-based extraction of Kenya’s historical road network from topographic maps is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Tanja Kramm et al. Kenya’s road network significantly influences environmental and socio-economic dynamics. High-quality road data is used to analyze its impact on various factors, including land-use, biodiversity, migration, livelihoods, and economy. Like many countries, Kenya faces challenges in the availability of accurate and detailed digital historical road datasets. Coverage: national (KE); published in 2025. Formats: Shapefile, Image. The data are held in GFZ Data Services and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
